overview.text: Iran vowed to end the U.S. naval blockade by all available means, while Trump said Iranian attacks have done no damage.
Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland, and NATO's Rutte sought to reassure eastern allies as Russian incursions into NATO territory increase.
A judge ruled Rep. Ilhan Omar could assert congressional privacy protections at the start of the search of her home.
The arrest of a father and daughter by ICE at Seattle airport has drawn outrage, and the family is speaking out.
CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler in a $44 billion deal combining two major cybersecurity firms.
Measles poses a growing risk to U.S. adults, including some vaccinated before 1989, medical experts say.

stories.headline: ✅ Spurs 123, Kings 107
stories.summary: Final · at Kings · Record 15-3

stories.headline: Judge says Omar could assert privacy protections during home search
stories.summary: A magistrate judge who authorized the federal search of Rep. Ilhan Omar's home ruled she was entitled to assert congressional privacy protections at the outset. Records show the government and judge debated constitutional implications.
stories.why: It tests limits on searches of sitting members of Congress.

stories.headline: A spokesperson says ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from exile in India on Dec. 16
Let's talk turkey: Here's how Thanksgiving meal costs have changed this year
stories.summary: Grocery costs have been on the rise, but food-price analysts say it's unclear if you'll spend more on the Thanksgiving meal this year. Some people are deciding not to host or are hosting fewer guests.

stories.headline: Iran vows to end U.S. naval blockade by 'all available means'
stories.summary: Iran said it will force the U.S. to lift its blockade. Trump acknowledged Iran's increasing attacks but said they have done no damage.
stories.why: Escalation in a naval standoff could widen the conflict.

stories.headline: No. 2 Official at F.B.I. Is Said to Be Retiring Before End of Year
stories.summary: The departure of Christopher G. Raia, a veteran agent, comes a few months after another deputy left the F.B.I.

stories.headline: How a Scientist Behind the Mediterranean Diet Got Caught in Trump’s War on Harvard
stories.summary: Walter Willett studies the link between diet and health, a high priority for Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. His grants were frozen anyway.

stories.headline: Russian incursions into NATO territory are increasing
stories.summary: NATO chief Mark Rutte is trying to reassure eastern European members after three Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland on Friday.
stories.why: Repeated spillover raises risks for the NATO alliance.

stories.headline: ICE arrest of father and daughter at Seattle airport draws outrage
stories.summary: Unmarked ICE agents arrested a father and his adult daughter at Seattle-Tacoma airport as passengers boarded a flight, and the scene was filmed. Some crew members asked to be replaced.
stories.why: Shows how immigration enforcement is playing out in public places.

stories.headline: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book
stories.summary: French woman says she will pursue legal action against publisher and author over use of photos taken by convicted husband Gisèle Pelicot has said she is “deeply shocked” that nude photographs of her had been used without her consent to…

stories.headline: States sue SpaceX over Grok generating child sex images
stories.summary: State attorneys general say Grok still produces child sexual abuse material and revenge porn. X says every Grok output is screened.
stories.why: Tests legal responsibility of AI companies for harmful output.

stories.headline: The rise and fall and rise again of Jensen Huang
stories.summary: Days after resigning while mired in scandal of extra-marital affairs, Nvidia's Jensen Huang is making a remarkable return.

stories.headline: Elon Musk Faces an A.I. Dilemma at SpaceX
stories.summary: Mr. Musk’s SpaceX is renting out computing power from its data centers to competitors, including Anthropic. That’s making it harder for his own A.I. effort.

stories.headline: Measles is a growing risk for U.S. adults
stories.summary: Unvaccinated people face the greatest danger, but vaccinated adults born before 1989 may no longer be sufficiently protected, medical experts said.
stories.why: Some adults may need to check their own protection.

stories.headline: CVS Health’s Planned Breakup Hasn’t Quieted Antitrust Critics
stories.summary: Lawmakers are warning that spinning off the health care conglomerate’s drugstores will not end scrutiny over its power.

stories.headline: H.I.V. Research Networks May Again Seek Federal Funding, With a Twist
stories.summary: The Trump administration restarted the process for funding four large research networks after postponing it earlier this year.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler in $44 billion deal
stories.summary: The two cybersecurity firms will combine as worries grow about hacks fueled by advances in artificial intelligence affecting companies and governments.
stories.why: Signals rising concern about AI-driven cyber threats.

stories.headline: They attended Trump's controversial meme coin dinner. It didn't go well
stories.summary: Trump held another meme coin dinner for top holders of his cryptocurrency — an event that has raised intense controversy. Here's an inside account from two guests who attended.

stories.headline: Britain's landlords are getting bigger. A two-tier rental market may follow
stories.summary: Increasing numbers of corporate landlords could usher in big changes for renters

stories.headline: SEC schedules vote on possible LSU expulsion
stories.summary: A dispute over RJ Luis has escalated into a legal and political fight between LSU and the SEC, with major penalties still possible.

stories.headline: 49ers win in Mexico, Bills stay on top in NFL Week 11
stories.summary: The San Francisco 49ers and Buffalo Bills remain the pacesetters in the NFC and AFC respectively.

stories.headline: Two goals in 15 games - what's going on with Gyokeres?
stories.summary: Arsenal have made an impressive start to the campaign but it has been a frustrating one for striker Viktor Gyokeres.

stories.headline: First Children's Booker prize reveals shortlist - and its child judges
stories.summary: The eight books in contention include War by Artemis Fowl author Eoin Colfer and Andrew Donkin.

stories.headline: Jefferson Airplane's Jorma Kaukonen says guitar has always been a 'great refuge'
stories.summary: Kaukonen helped define the sound of the '60s as the lead guitar player and a founding member of Jefferson Airplane. Now 85, he's still touring with his band Hot Tuna.

stories.headline: A First for a ‘Curious Incident’ Production: A Cast of Neurodivergent Actors
stories.summary: A company for neurodivergent actors steps up to a bigger stage with its full-spectrum model of inclusion.
